title: བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། ཚད་མ། མེ (Derge Tengyur, vol. 185)
shelf_note: A Pramāṇa commentary folio (refutation of establishing prior cognition through memory and arthāpatti, svasaṃvedana argument) in the Derge Tengyur Tshad ma section, as catalogued.

ocr_errors.problem: genitive འི read as ནི (line 5); both translations still construe it correctly

ocr_errors.image: ཕྱིས་ཀྱང་དོན་གྱིས་གོ་བས་མ་ཡིན་ཏེ (as far as the print can be read)
ocr_errors.problem: possible dropped instrumental ས; no change of sense

tr_errors_A.english: Even if experienced by another, that experience by another does not belong to another person because there is no experience; just as an external person has not experienced the object
tr_errors_A.problem: the closing example is garbled: 'does not belong to another person' and 'external person' (for ཕ་རོལ་པོ, 'the other person') obscure the point that the other's experience is not one's own

tr_errors_A.english: because the external object is hidden
To this, the commentary states: "That too..."
tr_errors_A.problem: the lemma is from the text being commented on, not 'the commentary'

tr_errors_A.english: because memory operates merely by its own occurrence
tr_errors_A.problem: loose: it proceeds by mere memory (as a recollection), not 'by its own occurrence'

tr_errors_B.english: because memory occurs as a mere mental event
tr_errors_B.problem: loose: the point is that it proceeds as mere memory, not as an inference

tr_errors_B.english: there is no experience established by implication other than the memory itself
tr_errors_B.problem: construal of a terse clause is somewhat muddled (A is equally so)

tr_errors_B.english: arguing instead that an experience must be self-aware to be valid
tr_errors_B.problem: summary slightly mis-states the thesis (cognition must be self-experienced for memory to be possible, not 'to be valid')

pages.prefer_reason: Both are faithful with no serious errors, but B renders the closing analogy of another person's experience coherently where A garbles it.

book_verdict: Clean Derge woodblock folio with a near-exact transcription; both English versions follow the argument faithfully, B being slightly clearer at the end of the page.
